author: reek
body: The emit-boundary prover decides whether a bounded field store needs its runtime check. It is handed the field's VALUE expression, not the scope around it, so until the range environment was carried on the codegen state a `let` between the proof and the use hid the proof: `direct` below elided its check and `via-let` -- the same arithmetic through a binding -- did not.

author: reek
body: Both functions must now report CDX4010. The `.diag` sidecar is the instrument: an elision is not visible in the answer, because a program whose checks are all emitted computes exactly the same thing, just slower. The `.expected` sidecar is the other half -- an elision that changes an answer is a wrongly elided check, which is the failure this whole path must never have.
